gap_rows.title: rwb-integration EFS hand-over deployment: the values, the alert identifiers, the dashboard series and the runbook have no source
gap_rows.source: WP B-P2-01; legacy RWB-E2-001 sections 4, 5 and 14; RWB-P2-E2001-OPS; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 32, 33 and 41; Architecture Decision Records v3 ADR-023; Non Functional Specification v3
gap_rows.description: The deployment of the step is a new artefact with no source text. (1) The legacy story names one feature flag and one hold time; nothing gives replica counts, resource sizes, probe paths and timings, lag thresholds, alert thresholds, consumer group name, retry intervals or the build ID format, so all of them are environment values and placeholders. (2) The legacy story raises a late-batch alert and an incident, and the FSD names MSG-P1-001, MSG-P2-001, MSG-P2-006 and MSG-P7-003; no source names a message id for a lagging hand-over group or for a consumed AceDataReady that started no run, so both carry the placeholder. (3) No source names the dashboard series of the hand-over or its dimensions; ADR-023 fixes observability per service and the six series here — accounts read, cases created, accounts linked, repeats, held, gap dates — are the default. (4) No source names the runbook entries, their owner roles or the runbook location. (5) The smoke-run fixture owner and the synthetic business date are not given.
gap_rows.evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-001 sections 4, 5 (X2, X6, X7) and 14 (MSG-P1-001, MSG-P2-007, MSG-P7-003, MSG-P2-006, MSG-P4-002); section 13 (feature flag rwb.integration.efs-handover). Architecture v5 slide 33 (rwb-comms and rwb-integration share the 16:00 window) and slide 41 (one login, one topic, one queue, one schema per service). Architecture Decision Records v3 ADR-023 (observability per service). Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-052, NFR-053 and NFR-054 (secrets, encryption, pipeline checks).
gap_rows.proposed: Fix the chart, the one consumer group, the registration step, the migration step, the six series, the four alerts and the four runbook entries in this story; keep every environment value in a values file and every missing message id as a placeholder until the Error and Message Standard names it; review the runbook with the on-call rota before the release date.

asm_rows.text: The rwb-integration service runs as one login created with the rwb_integration schema by the platform DB work (DP-02); the three stories of this key name it "the rwb-integration login" until the name is agreed, and carry it as a secret reference in the chart.
asm_rows.why: No source gives the login name and every DP-02 row requires one login per service; the legacy story ran on the shared recovery_svc login.
asm_rows.read: RWB-P2-E2001-APP sections 3, 10 and 13; RWB-P2-E2001-CON section 10; RWB-P2-E2001-OPS sections 10 and 11; DP-02 in Template and Rules section R5.5; Architecture v5 slide 41 (one schema and one login per service).
asm_rows.confirm: ACE DB owner and the platform DB story, before the rwb_integration baseline is created
asm_rows.impact: None on behaviour: the login is named by role and swapped for the agreed name without a content change.

asm_rows.text: Replica counts, resource sizes, probe paths and timings, the consumer group name, the lag and alert thresholds, the retry intervals, the build ID format and the smoke-run fixtures are environment values of the deployment; the lag alert and the no-start alert carry the identifier placeholder of GAP-0653 until the Error and Message Standard names them.
asm_rows.why: No source gives any of these values for this step, and the platform rule is that none of them is hard-coded in a chart, a dashboard or the runbook.
asm_rows.read: RWB-P2-E2001-OPS sections 3, 4, 5, 11 and 13; Template and Rules section R7.2 s17; Architecture Decision Records v3 ADR-023; Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-052 and NFR-054.
asm_rows.confirm: DevOps lead and the platform event owner, before the first SIT release
asm_rows.impact: Values change per environment without a code change; the two placeholder message ids follow the message catalogue when it is frozen.

asm_rows.text: The feature flag rwb.integration.efs-handover keeps the legacy name as the legacy reference only; in the target it is a flag of the platform flag library, and when it is off the worker and its consumer group are not deployed, so no run starts and no case, link or interaction entry is written.
asm_rows.why: The legacy story names the flag in service code and the platform default ruling moves feature flags to the platform library; the deployment needs one defined off behaviour.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E2-001 section 13 (feature flag rwb.integration.efs-handover); Template and Rules section R3 default ruling (feature flags to the platform library) and section R5.5 DP-15; Ownership Map v1 (feature_flag owner PLT); RWB-P2-E2001-OPS sections 4 and 13.
asm_rows.confirm: Platform library owner (RWB-PLT-E1047-CON) and the release manager
asm_rows.impact: The flag key and its off behaviour are configuration; no business value changes.
